static_traits.name: Zhang Di
static_traits.social_status: Keeping distance from coworkers with friends who know about his flying interest; has one close friend to confide in, but has not yet discussed this issue
static_traits.medical_history: Not yet experienced similar psychological problems; without prior psychotherapy; No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent thinking, fairly cooperative; speech rate Not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: After failing the first written flight exam, developing negative thoughts and a sense of failure related to 'learning to fly', leading to doubting their own ability and losing the motivation to keep trying.
basic_info.core_demands: These negative thoughts and feelings hinder my enthusiasm for learning to fly; I want to overcome this psychological barrier.
growth_experiences: While pursuing a Degree in funeral science, once encountered difficult courses and exams, initially struggled, but through persistent Learning and effort eventually passed the exams and graduated smoothly, showing an ability to gradually master new knowledge and pass exams in difficult situations.

core_beliefs: I am not smart enough/not good enough, cannot learn to fly
I am a failure/I cannot do it

special_situations.event: Failed the written test of the first flight course (occurred a month ago)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I fail the exam the first time, it shows I am not suited for flying and will never learn
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding retaking the test and continuing classes to avoid failing again and shame
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never learn to fly; I am not smart enough

special_situations.event: Whenever thinking of continuing flight lessons or seeing things related to airplanes
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I keep trying, I will only fail again and be proven not capable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduce contact with related stimuli, delay or stop acting to reduce Anxiety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will fail again; this is just a waste of time

special_situations.event: Interacts with friends or colleagues who know about their flying interest and is asked about progress
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If they know I failed, they will look down on me/think I am not capable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Social withdrawal and avoiding discussion of related topics
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are surely looking down on me

special_situations.event: Sees others successfully learning to fly or related publicity and cases
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If do not people can do it but I cannot, it shows I am just a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Use self-labeling to negate oneself, thereby stopping attempts
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: do not people can all learn, I am not capable

core_conflict.wish: Long to master flying skills and gain self-affirmation and others' recognition
core_conflict.fear: Fear of failing again, being humiliated or looked down upon by others, thereby confirming the worry of 'I am not capable'
defense_goal: Maintain safety and self-esteem by avoiding exams and related topics, reducing shame and Anxiety

object_relations.self_representation: A self with insufficient ability, prone to failure
object_relations.object_representation: Others with judgment and negate (who would look down on oneself)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When friends or colleagues bring up their flying interest and ask about exams or progress
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believe the other will look down on oneself like a judge (transference: projecting Self-denial onto others' intent)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Avoids topics, answers briefly, reduces eye contact, tries to end conversations and distances socially.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When needing to decide whether to retake the flight written exam or continue the flight course
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Take the belief 'I will fail again' as a reasonable justification, viewing continued attempts as an unwise move
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasize in a calm but firm tone 'now is not the time/I am not suited', using multiple reasons to justify the pausing behavior.

manifestations: Due to failure and shame, proactively keeps distance from friends and colleagues who know about their flying interest
Not yet expressing distress to close friends, choosing to bear it alone
outcomes: Social withdrawal intensifies the negative emotion cycle
Underutilization of the support system, increased inner sense of Loneliness

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Believing do not people will look down on oneself or mock failure
When asked about progress, presuming the other person's negative evaluation and avoiding communication

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Self-denial on the grounds of 'I am not smart enough/not suited'
Being overly cautious so as not to retake the exam or try, compressing one's space of choices

exception_events.target_problem: After failing the flight written exam, the visitor usually avoids retaking it and engages in Self-denial, thereby losing the motivation to continue Learning to fly.
exception_events.unique_outcome: While pursuing a Degree in funeral science, the visitor once encountered a difficult exam, initially performed not well, but then persisted in Learning and finally passed the exam, demonstrating the ability to still achieve breakthroughs in the face of setbacks.
exception_events.reason: Different approaches: sustained investment and practice; different understanding: viewing difficulties as part of the Learning process; situational support: knowledge and exam experience formed through past academic training.

positive_force: Has the experience and ability to persist in difficult situations and eventually pass exams (exam experiences during the degree)
Willing to seek help and change (proactively seeking counseling, open attitude)
Has one close friend to confide in (potential support resource)
negative_force: Catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking are prominent, tending to negate the not yet future entirely with one failure
Overgeneralization, mind reading and predicting the not yet future lead to avoidance of action
Social withdrawal and shame weaken external support, reducing the motivation to keep trying

target_behavior.function: Avoid potential failure and shame, temporarily relieving Anxiety and maintaining self-esteem
target_behavior.consequence: The goal of Learning to fly stalls, Negative emotions persisting and Reinforcement of Self-denial

target_behavior.behavior: Social withdrawal and avoiding discussion of flight progress with friends/colleagues
antecedent: Friends or colleagues mention their flying interest or ask about exam status
Flight-related topics arising in social settings
target_behavior.core_reason: Mind-reading and personalizing tendencies, worrying others look down on oneself, shame-driven defensiveness
target_behavior.function: Avoid being judged by others, reducing the immediate experience of shame and Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Underutilization of the support system, Increased sense of loneliness, negative beliefs maintained and repeatedly Reinforced
